type_ids_by_def_id.rumoca-ir-flat: Exact nominal type identity keyed by resolved declaration provenance.

type_name.rumoca-ir-ast: Declared type name from the component declaration. Used by post-instantiation type resolution to recover user-defined type IDs.

type_reference_root_def_id.rumoca-ir-ast: Resolved first-segment declaration of a qualified type reference. For `Medium.State`, this identifies the `Medium` class/package slot without recovering semantic structure from the rendered type name.

type_roots.rumoca-ir-ast: Canonical type roots for compatibility checks (alias/enumeration normalization). Keys are resolved type identities and values are canonical root type identities. Populated by typecheck_instanced for flatten-time type compatibility.

type_table.rumoca-ir-ast: All types in the compilation unit.

unconditional.rumoca-phase-structural: Residuals whose recording walk already yields a row, relevant to every variable.

unknown_count.rumoca-ir-solve: Number of projection unknowns (the leading slots).

unknown_names.rumoca-ir-solve: The block's unknowns by name, as the warning states them.
unknown_names.rumoca-phase-structural: The block's unknowns by name, the first few and a count of the rest.

unknowns.rumoca-ir-solve: Initialization unknowns may reside in either solver Y storage or parameter P storage.  Time and constant slots are invalid here.
unknowns.rumoca-phase-structural: Unknown names coupled in the block.

unlocalizable_guards.rumoca-ir-solve: Projection blocks whose own unknowns a relation under `noEvent` switches, with no root to localize it (SPEC_0044 ME-EVENT-008, ES016). Construction warns about each; a projection of such a block that fails is a typed fold of the relation, never a generic failure.

unresolved.rumoca-ir-ast: Names of modification targets the hierarchy does not resolve: every constant of such a name may be modified, so none is read at its declared value.

unrolled.rumoca-ir-solve: Per operation: the pass count when it is a loop emitted unrolled.

unused_captures.rumoca-ir-solve: The captures of each running conditional that neither arm loads, by operation.

update_jacobian_v.rumoca-ir-solve: Forward-mode JVP of the initialization update rows over `[solver-y | parameter]` seeds, row-aligned with `update_rhs`. It carries a seed through the bindings of the settled initialization view; `None` when a row has no derivative lowering.

update_levels.rumoca-ir-solve: The dependency levels of the parameter bindings.

update_order.rumoca-ir-solve: The dependency order of the parameter-binding programs.

updates.rumoca-ir-solve: Ordered aggregate patches. Each patch is rank-sized regardless of the carried tensor extent.

value.rumoca-ir-ast: The expression value of the modification. This is the resolved/evaluated form used for semantic checks during instantiation (e.g., conditional component activation).
value.rumoca-phase-structural: Signed terms whose sum is the stated value.

value_parameter_indices.rumoca-ir-solve: Runtime-managed P slot receiving the delayed value for each row.

value_reads.rumoca-phase-structural: Value expression roots evaluated at the tick.

value_type.rumoca-ir-dae: The constructed element type an empty array cannot infer.
value_type.rumoca-phase-structural: Structural value type (scalar kind and shape); declared quantity and unit types may differ across an equation, which already equates them.

values.rumoca-ir-solve: Value key to the registers holding its outputs.

variable.rumoca-ir-ast: The continuous-time state variable to reinitialize.
variable.rumoca-phase-structural: Closure identity, including a component when the source is projected.

variable_by_name.rumoca-ir-dae: Arena index of each reserved variable by name, so the duplicate-name check of a reservation is one lookup; internal only, never iterated.

variable_columns.rumoca-phase-structural: The unknown columns of each state and algebraic variable, in the dense variable order the incidence catalog uses (a state's columns are its derivative scalars, an algebraic's its value scalars); `None` for a variable with no unknown columns.

variable_declarations.rumoca-ir-solve: Canonical typed DAE declarations in the same dense identity order.

variable_final_flags.rumoca-ir-flat: Flat-output `final` qualifier flags keyed by variable name (MLS §7.2.6). When present and true, codegen should emit `final` before the declaration prefix.

variable_owners.rumoca-ir-flat: Authoritative variable-to-clock ownership, derived during insertion.
variable_owners.rumoca-phase-structural: Continuous owners that reference each variable in any coordinate form, in ascending owner order. A direct-state demotion rewrites exactly the owners that mention the demoted variable, so this is the set of rows the incremental incidence reprojects; every other row is reused unchanged.

variable_storage_runs.rumoca-ir-solve: Dense DAE variable ordinal to its first Solve storage slot. Scalar `k` of a variable is stored at `base + k` in the same column. This is the canonical cross-phase coordinate map; display names are not used to recover compiler identity.

variable_type_names.rumoca-ir-flat: Declared flat-output type name for each variable (e.g., Boolean, Integer, MyEnum). Keys match `variables` and values preserve resolved type identity for rendering.

variables.rumoca-ir-flat: Variables in this sub-partition and their owning source occurrences.

violated.rumoca-ir-solve: Whether a register or output the classification proved present was absent: the sharing declines as a whole.

whole.rumoca-ir-solve: Run start to exclusive run end; never overlapping, never adjacent.

whole_reads.rumoca-ir-solve: Carried values used other than by element access or update.

width.rumoca-ir-solve: The number of outputs the key was issued with.

witness.rumoca-phase-structural: One asserted equality incident to each variable, for candidate owners.

wrap.rumoca-phase-structural: `wrap(u) = ext(u)`: a Modelica body that reaches an impure callee.

y_indices.rumoca-ir-solve: Solver-Y indices of the block's unknowns.

y_start.rumoca-ir-solve: Target of `start`; `None` when the owning block pairs no Y index.

ArrayType.dims: Array dimensions (None means unknown size, e.g., from `:` subscript).

ClassDef.annotation: Annotation clause for this class (e.g., Documentation, Icon, Diagram)
ClassDef.array_subscripts: Array subscripts for type alias definitions (e.g., `type Vector3 = Real[3]`) Stores the `[3]` part as subscripts for later use in type resolution
ClassDef.causality: Causality from type alias definition (e.g., `connector RealInput = input Real`) Components of this type inherit this causality
ClassDef.class_type_token: Token for the class type keyword (model, class, function, etc.)
ClassDef.classes: Nested class definitions (functions, models, packages, etc.)
ClassDef.constrainedby: Constraining type for replaceable classes (MLS §7.3.2) If set, redeclarations must be subtypes of this type
ClassDef.constraining_modifications: Constraining-clause modifiers of a replaceable class whose merge into its base's modifiers needs types (MLS §7.3.2, §7.2.3): a declared binding over them, a `final` conflict, or a class with no single base. Parsing keeps them here; instantiation merges or refuses them when the class is used.
ClassDef.def_id: Unique identifier assigned during semantic analysis. None when first parsed, populated during name resolution.
ClassDef.description: Description string for this class (e.g., "A test model")
ClassDef.end_name_token: Token for the class name in "end ClassName;" (for rename support)
ClassDef.enum_literals: Enumeration literals for enum types (e.g., `type MyEnum = enumeration(A "desc", B, C)`)
ClassDef.expandable: True if the class is declared with the `expandable` keyword (MLS §9.1.3) Only meaningful for connector classes
ClassDef.external: External function declaration (MLS §12.9). Only meaningful for function classes.
ClassDef.is_final: True if declared with 'final' prefix (cannot be redeclared in derived classes) MLS §7.2.6: "A final declaration in an element modification prevents modification"
ClassDef.is_protected: True if this class is declared in a protected section
ClassDef.is_redeclare: True if declared with element-level `redeclare` prefix.
ClassDef.is_replaceable: True if declared with 'replaceable' prefix (can be redeclared in derived classes) MLS §7.3: "A replaceable element is an element that can be replaced by a different element"
ClassDef.location: Full source location spanning from class keyword to end statement
ClassDef.operator_record: True if the class is declared with the `operator` keyword (MLS §14) Only meaningful for record classes (operator record)
ClassDef.partial: True if the class is declared with the `partial` keyword
ClassDef.partial_derivative: Partial-derivative definition `f = der(g, u1, ...)` (MLS §12.7.2). A class carrying this has no body of its own: its meaning is the derivative of `g`, never `g` itself.
ClassDef.pure: True if the function is pure (no side effects). MLS §12.3. Only meaningful for function classes. Functions are pure by default. Set to false when declared with `impure` keyword.
ClassDef.purity_declared: True when the source declared `pure` or `impure` explicitly (MLS §12.3; external functions without an explicit declaration are deprecated, FUNC-032).
ClassDef.redeclare_target_def_id: Resolved inherited class slot replaced by this declaration (MLS §7.3). This is semantic identity, not a same-spelling heuristic. It is populated by name resolution after the containing class's extends graph is available.
ClassDef.scope_id: Scope created by this class for name lookup. None when first parsed, populated during name resolution.

ClassInstanceData.class_def_id: DefId of the class definition this instance was instantiated from.
ClassInstanceData.class_overrides: Effective replaceable class/package selections in this concrete class instance. Instantiation owns this context because it is the first phase where the complete modification environment and enclosing redeclares are known. Downstream phases must consume it directly instead of reconstructing virtual class identity from instance paths.
ClassInstanceData.initial_algorithms: Initial algorithm sections from this instance.
ClassInstanceData.instance_id: Unique identifier for this class instance.
ClassInstanceData.owner_component_id: Exact structured component occurrence whose type instantiated this class. The root model has no component owner.
ClassInstanceData.parameter_branch_selections: If-equations whose branch instantiation selected by evaluating component references (SPEC_0040 DAE-C22).
ClassInstanceData.qualified_name: Fully qualified name in the instance tree.
ClassInstanceData.resolved_imports: Resolved import map: short name → fully-qualified name (MLS §13.2). Collected from the class definition and its entire inheritance chain. Used during flattening to resolve imported short names (e.g., `pi` → `Modelica.Constants.pi`) instead of incorrectly qualifying them with the component instance prefix.
ClassInstanceData.source_scope: Lexical scope of the class declaration that produced this instance.
ClassInstanceData.source_scope_id: Resolved lexical scope of the class declaration that produced this instance.

ClassTree.def_map: Map from DefId to qualified name (e.g., "Package.SubPackage.Model"). Populated during the resolve phase for O(1) resolved definition lookup.
ClassTree.name_map: Inverse map from qualified name to DefId for O(1) resolved definition lookup. This includes non-class definitions such as components. Populated during the resolve phase alongside def_map.
ClassTree.scope_to_class: Each class scope's declaring class. Populated during resolve so later phases walk enclosing classes through the scope tree instead of re-parsing qualified names.
ClassTree.source_map: Source map for mapping file names to SourceIds. Populated during session build for multi-file diagnostics.
ClassTree.type_table: All types in the compilation unit.

Component.binding: The binding expression from `= expr` in declaration (e.g., `Real v = p.v - n.v`) Separate from `start` to preserve binding when both binding and start modifier are present.
Component.condition: Conditional component expression (e.g., `if use_reset` in `BooleanInput reset if use_reset`) None means the component is unconditional (always present)
Component.constrainedby: Constraining type for replaceable components (MLS §7.3.2) If set, redeclarations must be subtypes of this type
Component.def_id: Unique identifier assigned during semantic analysis. None when first parsed, populated during name resolution.
Component.each_modifications: Set of modification names that have the `each` prefix (MLS §7.2.5). When applied to array components, `each`-prefixed modifications apply the same value to every element, while non-`each` modifications distribute array values.
Component.final_attributes: Set of attribute names that are marked as final (e.g., "start" if `final start = 1.0`) When a derived class tries to override these attributes, an error should be raised
Component.has_explicit_binding: True if an explicit binding equation (= value) was provided in the declaration This distinguishes `constant Real c = 0;` (has_explicit_binding=true) from `constant Real c;` (has_explicit_binding=false, even though start may have a default)
Component.has_unapplied_redeclare: A nested component redeclaration has not yet been applied by Instantiate. Descendant dimension facts must remain unknown until it is consumed.
Component.inner: True if declared with 'inner' prefix (provides instance to outer references)
Component.is_final: True if declared with 'final' prefix (cannot be overridden in derived classes)
Component.is_protected: True if this component is declared in a protected section
Component.is_redeclare: True if declared with element-level `redeclare` prefix.
Component.is_replaceable: True if declared with 'replaceable' prefix (can be redeclared in derived classes)
Component.is_structural: True if this is a structural parameter (MLS §18.3) Structural parameters affect array sizes, for-loop ranges, or if-equation conditions and must be evaluable at translation time.
Component.location: Full source location for the component declaration
Component.modifications: Component modifications (e.g., R=10 in `Resistor R1(R=10)`) Maps parameter name to its modified value expression
Component.name_token: The token for the component name with exact source location
Component.outer: True if declared with 'outer' prefix (references an inner instance from enclosing scope)
Component.redeclared_by_modification: True once an `extends` modification has redeclared this inherited component (MLS §7.3, `extends Base(redeclare C a[2])`). This records the redeclaration's presence. Type and dimension application are separate from other component prefixes and modifiers.
Component.shape: Array dimensions - empty for scalars, e.g., [2, 3] for a 2x3 matrix Only populated when dimensions are known literal integers
Component.shape_expr: Raw array dimension subscripts (e.g., `n` in `Real x[n]` or `:` in `Real a[:]`) Used for parameter-dependent dimensions that need runtime evaluation Can be Subscript::Expression for explicit dimensions or Subscript::Range for `:`
Component.shape_is_modification: True if shape is from a modification (shape=x), false if from subscript \[x\]
Component.source_modification_each_flags: Parallel to `source_modifications` - true if the source modifier has an `each` prefix.
Component.source_modification_final_flags: Parallel to `source_modifications` - true if the source modifier has a `final` prefix.
Component.source_modification_redeclare_flags: Parallel to `source_modifications` - true if the source modifier is a redeclaration.
Component.source_modifications: Ordered source-form modifier arguments from the component declaration. These preserve the syntax inside `x(...)` before semantic component attributes are split into `start`, `binding`, `shape`, and `modifications`.
Component.start_has_each: True if the start modifier has `each` prefix (for array components)
Component.start_is_modification: True if start value is from a modification (start=x), false if from binding (= x)
Component.type_def_id: DefId of the component's type class (e.g., for `RealInput u`, this is the DefId of RealInput). None for built-in types (Real, Integer, Boolean, String). Populated during name resolution, used by instantiate phase for O(1) type lookup.
Component.type_id: Type of this component, resolved during type checking. None when first parsed, populated during type checking.

ComponentRefPart.def_id: Exact declaration reached by this segment. Resolve fills static paths; Instantiate fills segments deferred across replaceable-class boundaries before constructing instance IR.

ComponentReference.local: Whether this reference starts with a `.` (local lookup).
ComponentReference.parts: The parts of the reference (e.g., `a.b.c` has 3 parts).
ComponentReference.qualified_display_name: Non-semantic qualified display spelling. Resolution and identity proofs use only `parts`; this cache is ignored by equality and serialization. It spells the leading parts that stay on one reference when the reference is lowered — every part of an unsubscripted reference, and the parts up to and including the first subscripted one otherwise, always without subscripts. Lowering splits at that first subscripted part, so a spelling that covered more parts could not be attached to anything.
ComponentReference.span: Source span for this component reference.

Equation.span: Exact source range of the complete call, including delimiters.

Exposure.pinned: Declarations an outer modification already gave a value.
Exposure.unresolved: Names of modification targets the hierarchy does not resolve: every constant of such a name may be modified, so none is read at its declared value.

Expression.base: The expression to access the field from.
Expression.branches: List of (condition, expression) pairs for if and elseif branches
Expression.field_def_id: Exact declaration identity of the projected field after resolution.
Expression.is_partial_application: True for the grammar form `function F(bound = value)`. A partial application is a function value, not a call result. The parser must preserve that distinction through semantic checking.
Expression.name: The parameter name token (with source location)

Extend.base_def_id: Resolved reference to the base class definition. None when first parsed, populated during name resolution.
Extend.break_names: Component names that are deselected via `break` (MLS §7.4 Selective Model Extension). e.g., extends Base(break x, break y) would have break_names = ["x", "y"]
Extend.is_protected: True if this is a protected extends (MLS §7.1.2). Protected extends: `protected extends Base;`
Extend.location: Source location of the extends clause.
Extend.modifications: Modifications applied to the extends clause (e.g., extends Foo(bar=1)).

ExtendModification.each: True if the modification has `each` prefix (MLS §7.2.5).
ExtendModification.final_: True if the modification has `final` prefix (MLS §7.2.6).
ExtendModification.redeclare: True if the modification is a redeclaration (MLS §7.3).

ExternalFunction.annotation: Annotation arguments attached to the external clause (MLS §12.9.4). These remain syntax-preserving AST expressions so annotations such as `Library` and `Include` are not collapsed into rendered strings. The field is always written: the parsed-artifact cache decodes this type positionally, so no field may be omitted by value.
ExternalFunction.args: Arguments passed to the external function.
ExternalFunction.function_name: External function name (defaults to Modelica function name if not specified).
ExternalFunction.output: Output variable that receives the return value (if any).

Import.global_scope: True if import uses global scope (leading dot: `import .A.B.{C, D};`)
Import.names: All names imported from the package.

InstanceBranchSelection.conditions: The conditions evaluated, up to and including the one that held.
InstanceBranchSelection.origin: Qualified name of the class instance the if-equation came from.

InstanceConnection.family: Compact authoritative form for a regular vectorized connection. `a` and `b` above are the domain's first scalar member for diagnostic and compatibility views. Flattening derives all scalar members from this family at its input boundary.
InstanceConnection.scope: Scope where the connect statement was declared (flattened prefix). Used to determine the correct hierarchy level for flow sum equations. Empty string means root level.

InstanceData.attribute_source_scopes: Lexical scopes where attribute modifiers were written, keyed by attribute name (`start`, `min`, `max`, `nominal`).
InstanceData.binding_from_modification: True if binding came from a modification rather than declaration.
InstanceData.binding_source: Symbolic binding before evaluation for structural queries. Declarations and modifications retain their binding equation here when instantiation resolves a different value into `binding`. Flattening uses this source to preserve dependencies on changeable parent parameters.
InstanceData.binding_source_scope: Lexical scope where a modification-derived binding was written. Used during flattening to qualify symbolic modifier references according to MLS §7.2.4 without path-depth heuristics.
InstanceData.class_overrides: Active replaceable class/package redeclare overrides for this component instance. Keys are the DefIds of the redeclared local classes (e.g., `Medium`). Values retain the source alias text, effective target DefId, and the redeclare value component reference. Populated during instantiation so downstream phases can apply instance-specific package/class constants consistently (MLS §7.3).
InstanceData.component_ref: Structured resolved component reference for this concrete instance. This is the semantic carrier for downstream Flat/DAE phases. The rendered `qualified_name` remains useful for stable output spelling, but compiler logic should prefer this structured reference when available.
InstanceData.declaration_source_scope: Lexical scope where this component declaration was written.
InstanceData.description: Optional declaration description string (`"..."` after component declaration).
InstanceData.dims_expr: Unevaluated dimension expressions for parameter-dependent sizes. These are evaluated during flattening when parameter values are known.
InstanceData.evaluate: True if this parameter has annotation(Evaluate=true) or is declared final. Structural parameters can be evaluated at compile time for if-equation branch selection (MLS §18.3).
InstanceData.evaluate_refused: True if the declaration writes `annotation(Evaluate = false)`, which makes the parameter non-evaluable (MLS §4.5, §18.6).
InstanceData.fixed: Fixed attribute, scalarized per component element (MLS §4.8, §4.8.6). A single value broadcasts over every element; an array carries one value per element.
InstanceData.from_expandable_connector: True if this variable comes from an expandable connector (MLS §9.1.3). Unconnected expandable connector members without bindings are unused.
InstanceData.has_forwarding_class_redeclare: True when this component applies a self-forwarding class/package redeclare (e.g., `redeclare package Medium = Medium`) that is remapped to an active enclosing override during instantiation (MLS §7.3).
InstanceData.has_unapplied_redeclare: This occurrence or an enclosing occurrence retains an unapplied component redeclaration. Its dimensions cannot establish a shape proof.
InstanceData.is_connector_type: True if this component's type is a `connector` class (MLS §4.7). Per MLS §4.7, only flow variables in top-level public connector components count toward the local equation size. Models/blocks (like Delta) are NOT interface connectors even if they contain sub-connectors.
InstanceData.is_discrete_type: True if the base type is Integer or Boolean (MLS §4.5). These types are discrete by default even without explicit `discrete` prefix.
InstanceData.is_expandable_connector_type: True if this component's type is an expandable connector (MLS §9.1.3). Kept on the container instance because an empty expandable connector has no flattened descendants from which later phases could recover this semantic fact.
InstanceData.is_final: True if this component declaration has the `final` prefix (MLS §7.2.6). Used for preserving flat-output declaration qualifiers.
InstanceData.is_overconstrained: True if this variable belongs to an overconstrained connector (MLS §9.4). A connector is overconstrained if its type defines an `equalityConstraint` function.
InstanceData.is_primitive: True if this is a primitive type (Real, Integer, Boolean, String). False for class types (connectors, models, records, etc.) which are containers and should not appear as flat variables.
InstanceData.is_protected: True if this component is declared in a protected section (MLS §4.7). Protected components are not part of the public interface and their flow variables should not count as interface flows for balance checking.
InstanceData.oc_eq_constraint_size: The output size of the enclosing record's equalityConstraint function. E.g., 3 for Orientation (returns `Real[3]`).
InstanceData.oc_record_path: The path of the enclosing overconstrained record (MLS §9.4). E.g., "frame_a.R" for variables frame_a.R.T and frame_a.R.w. Used to group OC variables into VCG nodes for balance correction.
InstanceData.owner_class_id: Exact class occurrence that owns this component.
InstanceData.qualified_name: Fully qualified name in the instance tree.
InstanceData.source_location: Source location of the component declaration that created this instance.
InstanceData.type_def_id: DefId of the declared component type when available from resolve phase. Builtin types typically do not have a DefId.
InstanceData.type_id: Resolved type identity when known. Populated during instantiation/typecheck and consumed by flatten.
InstanceData.type_name: Declared type name from the component declaration. Used by post-instantiation type resolution to recover user-defined type IDs.
InstanceData.type_reference_root_def_id: Resolved first-segment declaration of a qualified type reference. For `Medium.State`, this identifies the `Medium` class/package slot without recovering semantic structure from the rendered type name.

InstanceEquation.origin: Origin of this equation (qualified name of the class it came from).
InstanceEquation.source_scope: Lexical source scope containing this equation.
InstanceEquation.source_scope_id: Resolved lexical source scope containing this equation.
InstanceEquation.span: Source span for error reporting. Never loses source location.

InstanceOverlay.array_component_declarations: Declarations with at least one array occurrence, including empty arrays that produce no component instances. This only vetoes universal scalar proofs; it does not identify or merge runtime occurrences.
InstanceOverlay.array_parent_dims: Array parent dimensions for expanded array components. When an array component like `plug_p.pin[3]` is expanded to indexed instances (`plug_p.pin[1]`, `plug_p.pin[2]`, `plug_p.pin[3]`), this map stores the parent path `plug_p.pin` with dimensions `[3]` for use in array equation expansion.
InstanceOverlay.class_type: MLS §4.7: The class type of the root model (model, connector, record, etc.)
InstanceOverlay.classes: Instance data for classes, keyed by their InstanceId.
InstanceOverlay.components: Instance data for components, keyed by their InstanceId.
InstanceOverlay.disabled_components: Disabled conditional components (MLS §4.8). Contains structured instance component paths whose conditions evaluated to false. These components and their sub-components should be excluded from flattening.
InstanceOverlay.each_modifier_bindings: Component bindings introduced by an `each` modifier (MLS §7.2.5). This remains structured instantiation metadata so flattening can preserve element-wise modifier semantics when an array component stays compact.
InstanceOverlay.effective_types: Concrete effective types produced after instance dimensions are resolved. Each component `type_id` names exactly one descriptor in this catalog after successful post-instantiation type checking.
InstanceOverlay.enumeration_type_roots: Canonical `TypeId`s proven by typechecking to denote enumerations. Effective component identities remain in `enumeration_types`; this root catalog also covers function values that do not have component occurrences in the instance overlay.
InstanceOverlay.enumeration_types: Effective type identities whose exact canonical root is an enumeration. Typecheck constructs this set from its resolved `TypeTable`; later phases never infer enumeration semantics from a rendered type name.
InstanceOverlay.inner_outer_to_parent_inner: Mapping from inner-outer component paths to their parent inner paths (MLS §5.4). When a component is declared `inner outer` (e.g., `inner outer StateGraphRoot stateGraphRoot`), it bridges two scopes: it serves as `inner` for children and as `outer` referencing the parent. Same-level connections involving the `inner outer` component should redirect to the parent's inner for flow equation scoping (e.g., `makeProduct.stateGraphRoot` → `stateGraphRoot`).
InstanceOverlay.is_partial: True if the root model is declared with the `partial` keyword. MLS §4.7: Partial models are incomplete and shouldn't be balance-checked.
InstanceOverlay.next_id: Number of occurrence identities allocated so far. Allocation is one-based because `InstanceId::UNSET` reserves zero, so this is also the last identity handed out.
InstanceOverlay.outer_prefix_to_inner: Mapping from outer-prefixed paths to their corresponding inner paths (MLS §5.4). When an outer component `initialStep.stateGraphRoot` references inner `stateGraphRoot`, equations/connections using the outer prefix are redirected to the inner path.
InstanceOverlay.root_description: Optional description string from the root class declaration.
InstanceOverlay.synthesized_inner_messages: Diagnostic messages attached to synthesized inner classes (MLS §5.4). Populated from each synthesized class's `missingInnerMessage` annotation when present, so the synthesized-inner warning can surface the class author's own guidance instead of a generic notice.
InstanceOverlay.synthesized_inners: Names of inner declarations synthesized during instantiation retry (MLS §5.4). Populated when `outer` components had no matching `inner` and automatic synthesis succeeded.
InstanceOverlay.type_ids_by_def_id: Exact nominal type identity keyed by resolved source declaration identity. This is producer-owned transition evidence from post-instantiation typechecking. Flattening uses it to type function values without interpreting their display names.
InstanceOverlay.type_roots: Canonical type roots for compatibility checks (alias/enumeration normalization). Keys are resolved type identities and values are canonical root type identities. Populated by typecheck_instanced for flatten-time type compatibility.

InstanceStatement.origin: Origin of this statement (qualified name of the class it came from).
InstanceStatement.source_scope: Lexical source scope containing this statement.
InstanceStatement.source_scope_id: Resolved lexical source scope containing this statement.
InstanceStatement.span: Source span for error reporting. Never loses source location.

Interface.class_kind: Specialized class kind (model, record, connector, function, etc.).
Interface.conditional: Whether this is a conditional component.
Interface.elements: Public named elements with their interfaces (recursive).
Interface.enum_literals: If this is an enumeration, the literal names in order.
Interface.external_object_name: If derived from ExternalObject, the full name.
Interface.is_class: Whether this represents a class (vs component).
Interface.operator_record_base: If this is an operator record, the base class identity.

InterfaceElement.is_class: Whether this is a class element (vs component).
InterfaceElement.name: Name of the element.

ModificationValue.each: True if the modification has `each` prefix.
ModificationValue.final_: True if the modification has `final` prefix.
ModificationValue.source: Optional source expression before eager resolution. When present, this preserves the symbolic modifier form (`k = parentK`) so downstream flat-output generation can keep parameter propagation relationships instead of hard-coding evaluated defaults.
ModificationValue.source_scope: Optional lexical scope where the modifier expression was written. MLS §7.2.4: component modifications are evaluated in the scope where the modification appears, which may differ from the modified component's scope.
ModificationValue.value: The expression value of the modification. This is the resolved/evaluated form used for semantic checks during instantiation (e.g., conditional component activation).

Name.def_id: Resolved definition ID (populated by resolve phase). For simple type names, this is the DefId of the class being referenced. For qualified type names (e.g., `Medium.AbsolutePressure`), this may be the DefId of the first part if full resolution fails (partial resolution). Partial resolution indicates the name is valid but depends on a replaceable type parameter that will be resolved during instantiation (MLS §7.3).

PartialDerivative.function: The differentiated function, looked up as in a short class definition.
PartialDerivative.inputs: The differentiated inputs, in application order.

Scope.inherited_members: Effective members contributed by resolved extends clauses. `InheritedMember::Ambiguous` records an ambiguous inherited name without choosing one base.

ScopeTree.predefined_members: Predefined names that remain visible at an encapsulated boundary.

State.block_instance: Reference to the block instance for this state.
State.is_initial: Whether this is the initial state (from initialState()). MLS §17.1: "One and only one instance in each state machine must be marked as initial."
State.name: State name.
State.nested_machine: Nested state machine (for hierarchical state machines).

StateMachine.id: Unique identifier for this state machine.
StateMachine.initial_state: The initial state (exactly one state must be marked initial).
StateMachine.qualified_name: Qualified name of the state machine instance.

StateMachineState.in_final_state: Whether the state machine is in a final state. MLS §17.2: "stateMachineInFinalState" - no outgoing transitions can fire.

Statement.outputs: Output variables being assigned (for `(a, b) := func(x)` style calls)
Statement.variable: The continuous-time state variable to reinitialize.

Transition.immediate: Whether the transition is immediate (fires at the same instant condition becomes true). Default: true
Transition.priority: Priority of this transition (MLS §17.1: "priority >= 1"). Lower number = higher priority. Default: 1
Transition.reset: Whether the target state is reset when the transition fires. Default: true
Transition.synchronize: Whether to synchronize with sub-state machines of the target state. Default: false

TypeTable.by_name: Map from type names to TypeIds for quick lookup.

ClockOwnershipEntry.kind: Which clocked coordinate role the owned variable was checked to have. Ownership is only ever minted after `own` rejects any other role, so the entry carries the outcome of that check rather than leaving a reader to re-derive it from the variable arena. The wire form omits it: replay re-issues the same checked operation and reproduces it.

Dae.active_discrete_scalar_count: DAE-owned derived metric: discrete coordinate scalars referenced by the finalized checked expression graph.
Dae.external_tables: Loaded native table descriptors (MLS §12.9.7 ExternalObject handles) that the constructor fold produced, keyed by the opaque integer id each handle parameter binds to. The solver interpolates these with its native table operators instead of calling foreign C code.

DiscreteValueOwnerEntry.observed: The targets are unread observations of a continuous-time definition, evaluated at every output point (SPEC_0022 EXPR-012).

ExprNode.owner: First projection node issued for this exact source call occurrence. Every result projection shares this identity and operand range.

ExprNodeWire.value_type: The constructed element type an empty array cannot infer.

ExpressionChildren.source_starts: Source ordinal each emitted record occupies; a model quotient owner record spans seven source ordinals, everything else one.

ExternalBodyEntry.native: The SPEC_0040 DAE-C30 compiler-defined body this interface is proven to match, derived by construction and never read from the wire.

ExternalFunctionBody.result: Output bound by the MLS §12.9 `output = symbol(...)` return form.

FixturePlan.real_eighths: Eighths, so the payload is a dyadic rational. The Real payload is deliberately not an arbitrary double. The workspace builds `serde_json` without its `float_roundtrip` feature (root `Cargo.toml` asks only for `preserve_order`), and its default number parser can land one ULP away from the correctly rounded value: reading back `-122.50221691932535` yields the neighbouring double, whose own shortest form is `-122.50221691932536`. That is a payload-fidelity defect of the name-tagged codec, not an ordinal defect — `bincode` carries the eight raw bytes and is unaffected — so this harness draws Reals from the domain both codecs represent exactly and leaves the defect to be fixed where it lives, in the workspace dependency declaration.

FrozenStorage.packed_value_counts: Packed scalar width of every value type, derived once at freeze.
FrozenStorage.record_field_prefixes: Per record type, the running sum of its field packed widths (one entry past the last field), derived once at freeze; `None` for a non-record or a record whose layout does not fit.

FunctionBuildState.active_fold: Lexically innermost open loop, or `None` at the function's top level. Every definition insertion reads this one field, so the issuing scope is recorded by the same act that issues the definition identity.

FunctionEntry.definition_scopes: Region that owned each definition when construction issued it. Element `n` answers for `definitions[n]`: `None` when the definition was issued by the function's top-level body, and `Some(scope)` for the lexically innermost open region. The vector always advances with `definitions`, so a definition identity and its issuing scope are one construction fact and cannot drift apart.

FunctionFoldEntry.continuation: A Boolean expression of the loop body scope, evaluated on the carried state at the start of each iteration; the first false value ends the fold with that state (a bounded `while`, MLS §11.2.3).
FunctionFoldEntry.iteration_locals: Function locals defined afresh inside each iteration. They belong to the transition region but are neither initialized from nor returned in the carried tuple.
FunctionFoldEntry.parent: Owner-local ordinal of the loop this one is lexically nested inside.

FunctionLoop.domain: The compact domain this transition iterates. A function body carries an optional domain because a body outside every loop has none. A loop capability is minted from the domain it was begun with, so it keeps that domain itself rather than reading the body's option back and asserting that a loop always has one.

FunctionStatementInput.continuation: The fold's continuation predicate, when it is a bounded `while`.

Storage.variable_by_name: Arena index of each reserved variable by name, so the duplicate-name check of a reservation is one lookup; internal only, never iterated.

VariableAttributes.causality: FMI-style causality metadata for downstream JSON consumers: one of `Input`, `Output`, `Parameter`, `CalculatedParameter`, `Independent` or `Local`, matching the values of FMI's `causality` attribute. This is the **exported** classification, not the source `input`/`output` prefix — see `declared_causality` for that, which an exported `Input` or `Output` must agree with (SPEC_0040 DAE-C24).
VariableAttributes.declared_causality: The source `input`/`output` prefix. An exported `Input` or `Output` causality requires the same declared causality (SPEC_0040 DAE-C24).
VariableAttributes.enumeration: The declaration of the enumeration type of an enumeration variable (MLS §4.9.5), so a consumer that exposes the variable names its literals.
VariableAttributes.evaluable: A `final` or `Evaluate=true` parameter or constant whose declaration binding is evaluable (MLS §4.5, §18.6; SPEC_0040 STRUCT-T10).

WireIds.next_wire_expression: Emitted-record cursor over `wire.expressions.nodes`. It trails `expressions.len()` (the source-ordinal cursor) by six for every replayed model owner.
WireIds.owner_expression_extra: Extra target expression nodes produced by owner replays (six per model owner).
WireIds.owner_operand_extra: Extra target packed operands produced by owner replays (three per model owner, two per function owner).
WireIds.quotient_replays: One slot per owner record in source order — the single global owner ordinal the stream markers name. Function owners hold a typed placeholder markers must reject; model owners hold the staged token consumed by their three markers and finished after roots.

Algorithm.span: Source span for error reporting. Never loses source location.
Algorithm.statements: The statements in this algorithm section.

AssertEquation.origin: Typed origin for scoped parameter/constant substitution.
AssertEquation.span: Source span for diagnostics and traceability.

BaseClock.source_span: Source span for the clock expression that introduced this base clock.

BaseClockPartition.clock: The base clock for this partition.
BaseClockPartition.discretized_at: Whether this is a discretized partition (contains der(), delay(), etc.). MLS §16.8.1: "If the partition contains a Discretized Variables, it is called discretized."
BaseClockPartition.source_span: Source span for the semantic owner that introduced this partition.
BaseClockPartition.sub_partition_index: Dense-position lookup for unique sub-clock IDs.
BaseClockPartition.sub_partitions: Sub-clock partitions within this base partition.
BaseClockPartition.sub_variable_owners: Variable occurrence and owning sub-clock ID.
BaseClockPartition.variables: Variables in this partition and their owning source occurrences.

ClockPartitions.base_partition_index: Dense-position lookup for globally unique base-clock IDs.
ClockPartitions.base_partitions: Base-clock partitions (execute asynchronously from each other).
ClockPartitions.continuous_partition: The continuous-time partition (if any). This contains equations without explicit clock associations.
ClockPartitions.source_span: Source span for the flattened model whose clock ownership is represented.
ClockPartitions.variable_owners: Authoritative variable-to-clock ownership, derived during insertion.

ConnectedVariable.connector_type: Reference to the connector type definition.
ConnectedVariable.is_inside: Whether this is an inside connector (sign = +1) or outside connector (sign = -1). MLS §9.2: "The sign is +1 for inside connectors and -1 for outside connectors."
ConnectedVariable.name: Globally unique variable name.
ConnectedVariable.source_span: Source span for the connector variable declaration, when available.

ConnectionGraph.nodes: Nodes in the graph (overdetermined type/record instances).
ConnectionGraph.optional_edges: Edges from connect() statements (optional - can be removed).
ConnectionGraph.required_edges: Edges from Connections.branch() (required - cannot be removed).

ConnectionSet.is_flow: Whether all variables in this set have flow prefix.
ConnectionSet.is_stream: Whether all variables in this set have stream prefix.

ConnectionSets.sets: All connection sets, indexed by a representative variable name.

EqualityConstraint.function_def: The function that computes the residual. Prototype: `function equalityConstraint(a: T, b: T) -> Real[n]`
EqualityConstraint.num_constraints: Number of scalar constraint equations (n in `Real[n]`).
EqualityConstraint.source_span: Source span for the equalityConstraint declaration or use site.

Equation.origin: Typed origin indicating where this equation came from.
Equation.scalar_count: Number of scalar equations this represents (MLS §8.4). For array equations like `x[n] = expr`, this is n. For scalar equations, this is 1. Used for balance checking per MLS §4.7.
Equation.span: Source span for error reporting. Never loses source location.

GraphEdge.in_spanning_tree: Whether this edge is in the spanning tree.
GraphEdge.source_span: Source span for the `connect`, `Connections.branch`, or related graph-edge source.

Model.assert_equations: Runtime assertion equations from regular equation sections (MLS §8.3.7). Assertions are preserved for flat output but do not contribute to DAE equation balance/unknown counts.
Model.branches: Branches from Connections.branch(a, b) calls (MLS §9.4). Required edges in the virtual connection graph.
Model.class_type: The class type of the root model (model, connector, record, etc.)
Model.definite_roots: Connectors with Connections.root() declarations (MLS §9.4.1). These are definite roots for overconstrained connectors, providing implicit equations that don't need to come from external connections. Stores the full path to the overconstrained record (e.g., "pin_p.reference").
Model.effective_types: Resolved effective type descriptors keyed by the exact `TypeId` stored on each concrete variable or aggregate instance.
Model.enum_literal_ordinals: Enumeration literal ordinal map (MLS §4.9.5, 1-based ordinals). Keys are canonical literal paths (e.g. `Modelica.Electrical.Digital.Interfaces.Logic.'1'`), values are integer ordinals used by runtime numeric evaluation.
Model.enumeration_declarations: Declaration of each enumeration type, keyed by the exact canonical type identity of `enumeration_type_roots` (MLS §4.9.5).
Model.enumeration_type_roots: Canonical type identities proven to denote enumerations.
Model.enumeration_types: Effective type identities whose exact canonical root is an enumeration.
Model.functions: User-defined functions used by this model (MLS §12).
Model.initial_assert_equations: Runtime assertion equations from initial equation sections (MLS §8.6, §8.3.7).
Model.initial_structured_equations: Structured source equation families for initial equations.
Model.instance_relations: Exact occurrence graph transferred from the instantiated tree. Source `DefId`s remain declaration provenance. Concrete containment and aggregate-to-materialization proofs use `InstanceId` exclusively.
Model.is_partial: True if the model is declared with the `partial` keyword. MLS §4.7: Partial models are incomplete and shouldn't be balance-checked.
Model.model_description: Optional description string from the root class declaration.
Model.oc_break_edge_scalar_count: Conservative scalar budget for VCG break-edge equations (MLS §9.4). Break edges are lowered to their declared `equalityConstraint` equations during connection generation. Balance accounting retains this metadata to validate the resulting equation inventory.
Model.optional_edges: Optional edges derived from connect() statements for overconstrained nodes (MLS §9.4). These are used together with `branches` when building the virtual connection graph.
Model.parameter_branch_selections: Branch selections flatten made by evaluating a parameter guard at translation (SPEC_0040 DAE-C22): an if-equation whose branches differ in equation count or in the variables they differentiate.
Model.potential_roots: Potential roots from Connections.potentialRoot(a, priority) calls (MLS §9.4).
Model.predefined_string_declaration: Exact Resolve identity of the predefined `String` declaration. Production flattening always supplies this from `ScopeTree`; downstream phases use it to distinguish the predefined conversion operator from a shadowing user declaration without rendered-name lookup.
Model.predefined_types: Exact canonical identities for predefined scalar types.
Model.record_instances: Resolved record containers retained for record-equation lowering. Record fields remain the authoritative Flat variables. This table only preserves the compact type identity discarded when containers expand.
Model.record_types: Resolved field layout for each record declaration used by an instance. This is type metadata, not callable-function reachability. Record equations use it to preserve one tensor equation per declared field.
Model.structured_equations: Structured source equation families for regular equations.
Model.top_level_connectors: Names of public top-level components whose class type is `connector` (MLS §4.7). Per MLS §4.7, only flow variables in top-level public connector components count toward the local equation size for balance checking. Components of type `model` or `block` (like Delta in transformers) are NOT interface connectors even if they contain connectors internally.
Model.top_level_input_components: Names of public top-level components declared with `input` causality. Fields of these components (e.g., `state.phase` from `input Record state`) are external inputs and should NOT be promoted to algebraic unknowns, unlike sub-component inputs from type interfaces (MLS §4.4.2.2).
Model.top_level_output_components: Public top-level components declared with `output` causality. Their record fields inherit the public interface prefix under MLS §4.4.2.2, independently of their runtime role (SPEC_0040 DAE-C24).
Model.type_ids_by_def_id: Exact nominal type identity keyed by resolved declaration provenance.
Model.variable_final_flags: Flat-output `final` qualifier flags keyed by variable name (MLS §7.2.6). When present and true, codegen should emit `final` before the declaration prefix.
Model.variable_type_names: Declared flat-output type name for each variable (e.g., Boolean, Integer, MyEnum). Keys match `variables` and values preserve resolved type identity for rendering.
Model.variables: All variables with globally unique names.

ParameterBranchSelection.kind: The structural use the read parameters fix.
ParameterBranchSelection.references: Per component reference its evaluated conditions read, the flat names it can denote, the innermost enclosing scope first.
ParameterBranchSelection.span: The selected if-equation, the declaration, or the for-equation.

RootStatus.priority: Priority value (lower = higher priority). Must be >= 0.

SpanningTree.edges: Edges included in the spanning tree.
SpanningTree.removed_edges: Edges removed from the spanning tree (will use equalityConstraint).
SpanningTree.roots: Root nodes selected for this tree.

SpanningTreeEdge.required: Whether this was a required edge (from Connections.branch()).
SpanningTreeEdge.source_span: Source span for the graph edge that produced this spanning-tree edge.

StructuredEquationFamily.domain: Compact index domain in source binder declaration order.
StructuredEquationFamily.equations_per_point: Uniform scalar-view equation count emitted by each domain point. A structured family is retained only when this count is uniform, keeping its metadata independent of domain cardinality.
StructuredEquationFamily.first_equation_index: First equation index in the corresponding flat equation vector.
StructuredEquationFamily.interiors: Whether the interior cells' scalar bodies are materialized in the equation vector, and when they are not, which construction owns the family's body. A family flattened with `FlattenOptions::materialize_structured_families = false` keeps full bodies only in its corner cells (base + one neighbor per binder); every other cell is a placeholder that no consumer may read.
StructuredEquationFamily.regular: Family-native classification: present when this family is a regular elementwise stencil whose array accesses are all affine in the binders, carrying the per-access stride table the Solve-IR lowering needs to build a compact `AffineStencil` without materializing one row per index tuple. `None` means the family is materialized the historical (scalar) way.
StructuredEquationFamily.template: The family's canonical comprehension body, captured by flatten before the loop is expanded. When present, downstream phases read the template directly (printing it as a `for`-comprehension, deriving strides, building a compact kernel) instead of reconstructing it from materialized corner cells. `None` for families flattened before this representation existed. See [`rumoca_core::ComprehensionTemplate`].

SubClock.source_span: Source span for the sub-clock expression.

SubClockPartition.id: Unique identifier within the base partition.
SubClockPartition.source_span: Source span for the semantic owner that introduced this partition.
SubClockPartition.variables: Variables in this sub-partition and their owning source occurrences.

Variable.binding_from_modification: True if binding came from a modification rather than declaration.
Variable.component_ref: Structured component reference that produced this flattened variable. The rendered flat name is display/protocol data. Compiler logic that needs path structure or resolved identity should use this reference instead of reparsing `name`.
Variable.connected: True if this variable is used in connection equations.
Variable.description: Optional declaration description string (`"..."` after declaration).
Variable.dims: Resolved array dimensions (preserved per SPEC_0007 and SPEC_0032).
Variable.evaluate: True if this parameter has annotation(Evaluate=true) or is declared final. Structural parameters can be evaluated at compile time for if-equation branch selection (MLS §18.3).
Variable.evaluate_refused: True if the declaration writes `annotation(Evaluate = false)`, which makes the parameter non-evaluable (MLS §4.5, §18.6).
Variable.fixed: Fixed attribute, scalarized per array element (MLS §4.8, §4.8.6). A single value broadcasts over every element; an array carries one value per element.
Variable.from_expandable_connector: True if this variable comes from an expandable connector (MLS §9.1.3). Unconnected expandable connector members without bindings are unused and shouldn't count as unknowns in the DAE balance calculation.
Variable.instance_id: Exact runtime occurrence identity allocated by instantiation.
Variable.is_discrete_type: True if this variable's base type is Integer or Boolean (MLS §4.5). Such variables are discrete by default even without explicit `discrete` prefix. This is used during variable classification to correctly identify discrete variables for the DAE balance calculation.
Variable.is_overconstrained: True if this variable belongs to an overconstrained connector (MLS §9.4). A connector is overconstrained if its type defines an `equalityConstraint` function.
Variable.is_primitive: True if this variable is a primitive type (Real, Integer, Boolean, String). Record-typed variables (like Complex with .re and .im fields) are not primitive. Non-primitive variables should not be counted as unknowns since their fields are counted separately. MLS §4.8: Balance checking uses expanded scalar counts.
Variable.is_protected: True if this component is declared in a protected section (MLS §4.7). Protected components are not part of the public interface and their flow variables should not count as interface flows for balance checking.
Variable.name: Globally unique flat name.
Variable.oc_eq_constraint_size: The output size of the enclosing record's equalityConstraint function. E.g., 3 for Orientation (returns `Real[3]`).
Variable.oc_record_path: The path of the enclosing overconstrained record (MLS §9.4). E.g., "frame_a.R" for variables frame_a.R.T and frame_a.R.w. Used to group OC variables into VCG nodes for balance correction.
Variable.source_span: Source span for the component declaration that produced this flat variable.
Variable.type_id: Reference to the type in the TypeTable.

WhenBranch.equations: Equations active when the condition triggers.
WhenBranch.span: Exact source span of this branch's condition.

WhenChain.span: Source span of the complete `when`/`elsewhen` equation.

WhenEquation.else_branch: Source-present else branch; `Some([])` is distinct from no else.

Accesses.whole_reads: Carried values used other than by element access or update.

AlgebraicClosure.block_states: The states each projection block's unknowns depend on.
AlgebraicClosure.owner: The projection block solving each algebraic (solver `state_count + k`).

AlgebraicProjectionBlock.alternate_charts: Additional admissible reconstruction charts for this block. Each chart re-partitions the block's `y_indices` into dependent (reconstructed) and independent (integrated) coordinates over the same `manifold_residual` rows; `tearing` remains the primary chart. A definitional first-integral manifold has no globally regular reduced chart, so a fixed partition folds when a dependent coordinate passes through zero. This bounded set of coordinate patches lets a runtime re-select a regular chart across such a fold. Empty for every single-chart block. An empty set is omitted from human-readable serialization by the manual [`Serialize`] below, so a single-chart block's JSON is byte-identical to a block that predates the field; positional binary formats keep the field so their fixed layout still round-trips.
AlgebraicProjectionBlock.tearing: Structural tearing of this coupled block. When present, the runtime projection iterates Newton only over the tear variables and recovers the remaining unknowns by ordered back-substitution, in the sense of Elmqvist and Otter, ESM'94, and Cellier and Kofman, "Continuous System Simulation", chapter 7. OpenModelica causalizes the same loops the same way, which makes it a behavioural cross-reference rather than the authority for the method. Absence selects the dense block Newton over every unknown.

Assigners.by_target: Every exact assignment target, sorted, with the assignments issuing it.

BlockTearing.causal_steps: Back-substitution steps evaluated in order once the tear variables are fixed: each step solves its residual row for its unknown.
BlockTearing.residual_rows: Residual rows forming the reduced Newton system driven to zero over the tear variables. A subset of the block's `rows`.
BlockTearing.tear_y_indices: Solver-Y indices iterated by the reduced Newton. A subset of the block's `y_indices`, equal in count to `residual_rows`.

Builder.closed: Values of segments closed at the cap.
Builder.violated: Whether a register or output the classification proved present was absent: the sharing declines as a whole.

CausalStep.coefficient: Why the step's isolated coefficient is bounded away from zero; set by construction and trusted by every executor (SPEC_0043 §4).

CoSimulationController.default_tolerance: Relative and absolute tolerance of the local error when the importer defines none (the FMI setup tolerance replaces it otherwise); equal to the native simulation's default tolerance.
CoSimulationController.max_substeps: Attempted substeps one communication step may take before it is discarded.
CoSimulationController.min_factor: Smallest and largest factor one substep may change the step size by.

ColoredLaneCall.placements: `(lane, program output offset, destination offset)` of every value this evaluation places.

ComputeNode.lhs_pattern: Sparsity of the lhs (A) operand.  `Dense` unless the lowering phase can statically prove a sparser structure.
ComputeNode.matrix_pattern: Constructor-derived structural pattern of the square coefficient matrix. Runtime values never redefine this relation.
ComputeNode.rhs_pattern: Sparsity of the rhs (B) operand.  `Dense` unless statically known.

ComputeOutputImage.invocations: Cardinality issued by the canonical domain validator.

ContinuousRefreshOwners.native_assignment: The stateless native value schedule or why the problem has none; `None` until [`issue_native_assignment_schedule`] runs.

ContinuousSolveArtifacts.implicit_jacobian_v_scalar: Per-row forward-mode AD JVP of the *scalarized* `implicit_rhs`, row-aligned with successful `to_scalar_program_block(implicit_rhs)` output (and hence with the algebraic refresh plan's `row_idx`). Used by the state-only path to propagate the state seed through the algebraic projection (`d(alg)/d(state)`). Distinct from the tensor `implicit_jacobian_v`, whose scalarization is not row-aligned when the system has linear (`LinSolve`/`MatMul`) blocks.
ContinuousSolveArtifacts.structural: Constructor-derived metadata; canonical Solve replay reconstructs it.

ContinuousSolveSystem.manifold_projection_plan: Connected state-coordinate blocks used to project accepted numerical steps onto `manifold_residual = 0`. Blocks may have more state coordinates than residual rows; runtimes use a minimum-norm correction.
ContinuousSolveSystem.manifold_residual: Lower-order holonomic and velocity residuals retained when structural index reduction replaces them with acceleration-level equations.
ContinuousSolveSystem.reduced_chart_set: Admissible reduced state-selection charts for a definitional first-integral coordinate group. A conserved first integral has no globally injective reduced chart: the fixed primary basis folds when one of its dependent coordinates passes through zero. Each chart in this bounded set is one alternate Dependent/Independent column selection of that group, expressed in the same solver-Y space as the primary basis, so a runtime can re-select a regular chart across such a fold. Chart index zero is the primary basis. An empty set is dropped from human-readable serialization, so a model with no chart set has byte-identical JSON to one that predates the field; positional binary formats keep the field so their fixed layout still round-trips. Each alternate plan travels as a delta against this system (see `continuous_wire`).
ContinuousSolveSystem.refresh_owners: Exact checked refresh owners issued during Solve construction. Runtime adapters prepare these schedules but never discover or filter them.
ContinuousSolveSystem.unlocalizable_guards: Projection blocks whose own unknowns a relation under `noEvent` switches, with no root to localize it (SPEC_0044 ME-EVENT-008, ES016). Construction warns about each; a projection of such a block that fails is a typed fold of the relation, never a generic failure.

ContinuousStructuralArtifacts.state_jacobian: The state Jacobian `d(der)/d(states)`, derived from `derivative` through the algebraic projection ([`StructuralPattern::derive_state_jacobian`]).

Dependencies.exact: Exact relations on leaves that no whole-input run covers.
Dependencies.terms: Total relation terms held per exact leaf.
Dependencies.whole: Run start to exclusive run end; never overlapping, never adjacent.

DiscreteSolveArtifacts.guarded_jacobian_v: Program `i` differentiates guarded assignment `i`, output for output.
DiscreteSolveArtifacts.structured_jacobian_v: Row-aligned with the scalar view of [`DiscreteSolveSystem::structured_rhs`].

DiscreteSolveSystem.clock_owners: Periodic activation owner for each discrete row. `None` denotes an ordinary event-iteration row. A clock-owned row is evaluated only when the referenced exact lattice ticks.
DiscreteSolveSystem.clock_partition_intermediate_clocks: Exact consumer clock domains for each intermediate output row. A row is refreshed iff at least one domain in its non-empty set ticks. The structural same-tick proof issues these sets; execution only replays them and never reconstructs dependency liveness.
DiscreteSolveSystem.clock_partition_intermediate_targets: Work-state storage slot for each `clock_partition_intermediates` output row (row-aligned).
DiscreteSolveSystem.clock_partition_intermediates: Exact causal definitions of the algebraic intermediates that sit on a same-tick path between two ordered producers (for example an alias chain `slow = fastAlias; fastAlias = fast`). Each output row refreshes one scalar coordinate into private work state only — intermediates become visible to later producers without committing unrelated targets.
DiscreteSolveSystem.clock_partition_order: SPEC_0040 SOLVE-C57 (implementing toward SPEC_0046 SDO-001/SDO-002): the construction-issued same-tick execution order for every clock-owned discrete producer. Rank is the vector position — an issued value. The runtime executes the steps in this order against private work state so an ordinary same-instant read observes this tick's value while `pre`/`previous`/ `sample(u)` reads keep their history lanes; the complete final target tuple still commits atomically after the last step. Equation-shaped producers owned by a DAE-C21/SOLVE-C55 event transaction are excluded; the complete transaction replaces them as one opaque outer-producer step. A runtime must never reconstruct this order from targets, names, spans, provenance, or program shape.
DiscreteSolveSystem.event_transactions: Model-level event algorithms remain one ordered typed transaction across mixed discrete Real and discrete-valued storage.
DiscreteSolveSystem.guarded_assignments: Correlated guarded updates retain one compact result program and one ordered target-range catalog. Scalar coordinate rows are derived only by evaluator/backend adapters.
DiscreteSolveSystem.integrator_history_effects: Compiler-derived effect of changing each scalar update target on an integrator's continuous multistep history. This vector is row-aligned with `rhs`. A runtime may join the effect with exact update changes, but must not recover it from row position or model identity.
DiscreteSolveSystem.observation_refresh_reads_y: Construction certificate: at least one selected scalar observation row reads Y storage and therefore must be rechecked after continuous algebraic projection. False proves that one discrete refresh followed by one projection is the complete public fixed point.
DiscreteSolveSystem.post_commit_assignment_rhs: Relation-free root-driven assignments that remain valid after event `pre` history has committed.
DiscreteSolveSystem.post_commit_assignment_runtime_rows: Runtime-row owner copied by each post-commit row. Shape validation proves the copy is exact and the owner is relation-free.
DiscreteSolveSystem.runtime_assignment_roles: Compiler certificate for whether each runtime assignment evaluates a relation (directly or through another runtime assignment).
DiscreteSolveSystem.structured_rhs: Compact B.1c maps. Scalar owners remain in `rhs`; a structured owner is represented exactly once here and is scalarized only by evaluation or backend adapter APIs.

EventIterationPlan.schedule: How every executor walks the iteration (SPEC_0044 ME-EVENT-006).

EventWrites.opaque: An event owner whose targets are not enumerated here (an aggregate transaction or a structured update) exists, so no bound is claimed.
EventWrites.parameters: Parameter storage indices an event writes: discrete values, relation and condition memory, `pre` copies, and clock activation lanes.
EventWrites.solver_y: An event writes a solver coordinate (a state reset or algebraic update).

ExactRefreshAssignmentProgram.assignment_leaf_dependencies: Issued once every program exists; see [`LeafDependencies`].

Family.empty: Issued from the operation rule and captured source witnesses.

FaultFlow.pass_lanes: For a loop operation: the exactness of the operations of one pass.

FmiCCodegenView.binding_execution: Whole-program evaluation and lifecycle-specific commits share one owner.
FmiCCodegenView.discrete_order: The evaluation orders of the parameter-determined discrete rows.
FmiCCodegenView.state_reinitializations: Per published declaration: whether a source event may reset its state.
FmiCCodegenView.update_levels: The dependency levels of the parameter bindings.
FmiCCodegenView.update_order: The dependency order of the parameter-binding programs.

FmiEventIndicatorInventory.plan: The positional reading of `sources` every executor uses: where each position reads its value, the side an exact zero takes, and the relation memory a crossing reseeds (SPEC_0044 ME-EVENT-005).

FmiVariableInput.declared_causality: The declared prefix where it differs from `causality`; construction refuses one the exported causality already states.
FmiVariableInput.enumeration: The declaration of the enumeration type of an `Enumeration` declaration (MLS §4.9.5).
FmiVariableInput.evaluable: A parameter whose value is fixed at translation (MLS §4.5, §18.3).
FmiVariableInput.text_start: The literal start of each scalar of a `String` declaration.

FunctionFoldProgram.continuation: A bounded `while` fold's predicate (MLS §11.2.3), evaluated on the carried tuple and captures before each pass; the first false value ends the fold with that tuple. It reads no binder.

IndexedRun.reach: The largest `end` among this run and every run sorted before it.

IndicatorPlanInputs.model_root_count: Length of the model root prefix of that vector.
IndicatorPlanInputs.root_value_count: Length of the runtime root-condition vector: model roots then delays.

InitialSensitivityPlan.rows: Residual rows the projection plan solves.
InitialSensitivityPlan.seeds: Seed index of each slot over `[solver-y | parameter]`.
InitialSensitivityPlan.slots: Unknown slots, projection unknowns first, then update targets.
InitialSensitivityPlan.unknown_count: Number of projection unknowns (the leading slots).

InitializationProjectionBlock.scales: The Newton scale of each unknown, aligned with `unknowns`.
InitializationProjectionBlock.unknowns: Initialization unknowns may reside in either solver Y storage or parameter P storage.  Time and constant slots are invalid here.

InitializationProjectionPlan.iterates_discretes: Whether a planned row reads a discrete coordinate the projection holds at its current value. The runtime then alternates the projection with the discrete assignments until the discrete values stop changing, the fixed point of the MLS §8.6 mixed initialization system.

InitializationSolveArtifacts.structural: Constructor-derived metadata; canonical Solve replay reconstructs it.
InitializationSolveArtifacts.update_jacobian_v: Forward-mode JVP of the initialization update rows over `[solver-y | parameter]` seeds, row-aligned with `update_rhs`. It carries a seed through the bindings of the settled initialization view; `None` when a row has no derivative lowering.

JacobianStructure.column_rows: The immutable pattern's rows per column, derived only when a consumer needs the coordinate view. Clone keeps the established owned-cache behavior: an initialized view is copied; an unused view stays unused.
JacobianStructure.compact: Compact storage layout shared by every matrix in this pattern.

LanePrograms.dependencies: Per-output seed dependencies of each JVP program read so far; `None` when the program's dependencies are not derivable.

LinearOp.updates: Ordered aggregate patches. Each patch is rank-sized regardless of the carried tensor extent.

LoopFlow.unrolled: Per operation: the pass count when it is a loop emitted unrolled.

ParameterClassification.baked_starts: Selected parameter to the states whose `start` expression reads it and that the initialization neither solves nor updates: the lowered model fixed those starts as constants.

PeriodicClock.activation: The hidden parameter that reads 1 while this clock ticks.

PreParamBinding.clock_schedule: Owning periodic clock for MLS §16 `previous()` history. `None` denotes ordinary Modelica `pre()` history and is committed after every event. A scheduled binding is committed only when this clock ticks, so unrelated roots and other clocks cannot advance its history.

ProgramBuilder.map: Program register to the segment register holding its value.

ProjectionJacobianApplication.compact: The compact storage order of the block pattern every placement addresses.

ProjectionStageData.index: Fixed with `stages`; every constructor derives it from them.

ReadFlow.register_listed_twice: Whether the last reader lists the register more than once.

ReducedChartPlan.artifacts: Runtime-executable continuous solver artifacts of the alternate basis: its AD Jacobian-vector products and derived structural patterns. Derived data, rebuilt after decode by the owning phase, so it is skipped by every serializer and defaults to empty until re-materialized.
ReducedChartPlan.delta: The faithful wire delta of this plan against the primary system, issued once by [`ChartPlanDelta::diff`] at construction or kept from decoding.
ReducedChartPlan.refresh_owners: Issued continuous refresh owners of the alternate basis. Serialized and decoded through [`ContinuousRefreshOwners`]'s own checked replay.

Regions.spans: `(start, register count)` of each region in the source program.

RootBracket.low_weight: The Illinois weights of the indicator values held at each end.

RootLocationPlan.fallback_scan_resolution: The scan resolution of an experiment without a finite positive width.
RootLocationPlan.minmax_slack: Evaluations the refinement may take beyond the bisection count of its bracket: the `n0` of the minmax projection.
RootLocationPlan.refinement_iteration_cap: Refinement evaluations a bracket may take before location fails typed. It exceeds every bound the minmax projection proves for a bracket at most `2^(cap - slack)` location tolerances wide.
RootLocationPlan.roundoff_epsilons: Machine epsilons, scaled by the interval's time magnitude, that make up the roundoff of one accepted interval.
RootLocationPlan.scan_fraction: Adjacent indicator samples are at most this fraction of the experiment width apart, independent of the output cadence (SPEC_0044 §6).
RootLocationPlan.sliding_gap_fraction: The widest gap between two state events of one indicator, as a fraction of the scan resolution, that continues its streak.
RootLocationPlan.sliding_streak: Consecutive close state events of one indicator that make it slide ([`SlidingModes`]).

RowSegment.y_start: Target of `start`; `None` when the owning block pairs no Y index.

ScalarEventProfile.condition_memories: The parameters actions read at their event-entry value.
ScalarEventProfile.condition_memory_rows: Per discrete output: whether it is a condition memory, the rows initialization seeds with `pre` following the current value.
ScalarEventProfile.discrete_input_runs: Source storage runs of discrete-valued external inputs. A discrete-time input changes only at events (MLS §4.5), so a change the importer makes between Co-Simulation steps is an event at the next step's first instant.
ScalarEventProfile.discrete_targets: Per discrete output: its parameter target.
ScalarEventProfile.guarded_clocks: Per guarded-assignment output: the periodic clock that owns it, which gates it to that clock's ticks and to the first pass of an event.
ScalarEventProfile.guarded_targets: Per guarded-assignment output, in program order: its target.
ScalarEventProfile.iteration_lanes: The pre bindings (indices into `pre_bindings`) an event pass advances and whose settlement ends the iteration.
ScalarEventProfile.observation_reads_y: Whether an observation row reads a solver coordinate, so the algebraic refresh and the rows alternate until they agree.
ScalarEventProfile.observation_rows: Per discrete output: whether a public observation recomputes it from the observed coordinate (an unread B.1c owner, SPEC_0022 EXPR-012).
ScalarEventProfile.pre_bindings: Destination and source of every pre binding, in binding order.
ScalarEventProfile.pulse_rows: Pulse-memory outputs and their checked producing programs. Only these programs are evaluated when the event releases its clock pulses.
ScalarEventProfile.root_neighborhoods: Per root output: the outputs reading a coordinate it reads, itself included (ME-EVENT-008 mode search).
ScalarEventProfile.roots: Per root output: whether and how it is evaluated in Event Mode.
ScalarEventProfile.runtime_targets: Targets of the runtime assignments and of the post-commit assignments, in output order.
ScalarEventProfile.schedule: The event iteration schedule the component walks (ME-EVENT-006).
ScalarEventProfile.time_events: The time events the component announces and stops at.

ScalarEventRoot.algebraic_dependent: Whether the relation memory is refreshed from the algebraic coordinate after the event commit.
ScalarEventRoot.memory: The relation-memory parameter this root writes, if any.

ScalarProgramData.program_register_counts: Construction-owned execution capacity for each stored program. This proof is rebuilt on wire replay and deliberately is not serialized as a second source of truth.

ScalarProgramValidationCache.tangent_lanes: Admit tensor operations of up to [`MAX_TENSOR_LANES`] interleaved lanes (a tangent-lane program) rather than one primal or two dual lanes.

Segment.stored: Slots stored so far and the register holding each.
Segment.terms: Term of every register the segment wrote.
Segment.values: Value key to the registers holding its outputs.

SlidingModes.intervals_since_event: Intervals begun since the latest state event.
SlidingModes.last_event: Time of each indicator's latest state event.
SlidingModes.sliding: Whether a domain change of each indicator in the current interval applies without refinement.
SlidingModes.streak: Consecutive close state events of each indicator, ending at `last_event`.

SolveAlgorithmBlock.function_sources: The checked function each owner refines, in owner order.
SolveAlgorithmBlock.functions: The block's functions as pure-call owners, which every method may call.
SolveAlgorithmBlock.status_bindings: Each function owner's status channels, in owner order.

SolveCallDependency.coordinates: None explicitly denotes dependence on the whole input leaf.

SolveCallSiteCount.callee_provenance: Source span of the callee's call occurrence.
SolveCallSiteCount.sites: Static `Call` operations in the caller's body, regions included.

SolveClockPartition.activation_parameter_indices: Hidden Boolean-as-Real P slot for each typed periodic clock. The runtime derives each value from the schedule at the current event instant. These lanes make clock leaves computable inside mixed condition DAGs without creating another clock or row owner.

SolveDelayPartition.delay_max_rhs: Maximum retained history horizon. When source `delayMax` is omitted, this row is identical to the corresponding delay-time row.
SolveDelayPartition.delay_time_rhs: Delay amount evaluated at the query time.
SolveDelayPartition.source_is_discrete: Whether the source uses piecewise-constant history rather than linear interpolation between accepted points.
SolveDelayPartition.source_rhs: Current-value expressions whose accepted values populate history.
SolveDelayPartition.value_parameter_indices: Runtime-managed P slot receiving the delayed value for each row.

SolveEventAction.assertion_projection: Wire recipe for the checked projection of one source invocation. A detached recipe grants no authority; the observer borrows its exact model table, source program and ordered action inventory together.
SolveEventAction.clock_owner: Exact periodic owner for a clock-scoped action. `None` denotes an ordinary state/event action. A clock-owned action is eligible only when this schedule ticks; the condition program retains its activation lane as a local semantic guard.

SolveEventPartition.condition_memory_parameter_indices: Hidden P slots that retain the previous value of each DAE condition. Event-action programs read these slots to distinguish a rising edge from a condition that merely remains true across an unrelated event.
SolveEventPartition.root_relation_refresh_roles: Compiler certificate describing which root memories may participate in post-commit algebraic coupling.
